findings.title: targetMeanPrice/targetMedianPrice scaled by financial FX factor, not trading factor
findings.description: CCY_DENOMINATED_METRICS includes targetMeanPrice and targetMedianPrice, which are FX-scaled via scale() using the financial-reporting `factor`. But analyst price targets are quoted in the TRADING currency (same unit as price.regularMarketPrice), which the code deliberately leaves UNSCALED (lines 400-404 keep price in trading currency). The inline comment (lines 419-421) asserts targets are 'in the reporting currency (same as prices)' - but prices are NOT in reporting currency for ADRs and are not converted at all.
findings.mechanism: For an ADR like TSM (reporting ccy TWD, trading ccy USD), `factor` = TWD->USD (~0.031). targetMeanPrice comes back from Yahoo in USD (trading ccy). scale() multiplies the already-USD target by 0.031, producing a target ~32x too small. currentPrice stays in USD. analyst-upside = target/price is then ~32x wrong. Same defect for GBp pence LSE names where factor = GBP_rate/100.
findings.reproducer: Snapshot with meta.reportingCurrencyOriginal='TWD', metrics.targetMeanPrice from Yahoo in USD. After _convertSnapshotToUSD, targetMeanPrice.value is multiplied by the TWD financial factor while price.regularMarketPrice is unchanged. Compare upside ratio against a US-listed control.
findings.impact: Every analyst-upside / price-target ratio is silently wrong for all non-USD reporting tickers (ADRs + LSE pence + any foreign reporter). Magnitude equals the trading-vs-reporting FX ratio (up to ~100x for pence).
findings.suggested_fix: Route targetMeanPrice/targetMedianPrice through scaleTrading() (tradingFactor) instead of scale(), mirroring marketCap. They are price-unit metrics, not reporting-currency metrics.

findings.title: Universe shrinkage (skipped-mcap / fx-unknown) only logged per-ticker, no aggregate survivor-bias alarm
findings.description: When a full pull yields fxConversionFailed (status 'fx-unknown') or fails the MIN_MCAP floor (status 'skipped-mcap'), the existing on-disk snapshot is unlinkSync'd and the ticker is recorded in results[] with an INFO log. The price-only path (line 1580-1583) also deletes snapshots below the floor. There is no run-level counter comparing deletions against a threshold or against the prior run, so a systematic Yahoo schema/FX change that silently drops hundreds of tickers from the universe produces no HIGH alert - only a flood of individual INFO lines.
findings.mechanism: Per-ticker INFO + results.push(status). No run-level survivor-bias gate. If MIN_MCAP_USD env is mis-set, or an FX currency goes stale leaving no rate, whole regions/currencies get deleted with no aggregate signal.
findings.reproducer: Set MIN_MCAP_USD=2e10 (impossibly high) -> entire universe deleted snapshot-by-snapshot, run still 'succeeds' with results full of skipped-mcap; no aggregate alarm.
findings.impact: Silent universe shrink = survivor bias in all downstream screening. Especially dangerous on the price-only fast-path (~80% of pulls) where a below-floor mcap deletes the snapshot mid-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Aggregate counts of skipped-mcap + fx-unknown + price-only-floor deletions; emit a HIGH alert when the deletion ratio exceeds a baseline (e.g. >5% of universe, or >2x prior run), analogous to field-coverage drift detection.

findings.title: Field-coverage drift detector blinded for ~7d by price-only persistence of stale fundamentals
findings.description: On the ~80%-hit price-only path, _quality.grade is preserved (Tag 232c-12) but the fundamentals arrays (annual.*/timeseries.*) are NOT re-read from Yahoo - the OLD persisted arrays are written back unchanged. The drift detector (field-coverage.js computeCoverage) reads persisted snapshot fields, so a live Yahoo schema drop on a fundamentals field is masked until each ticker's slow full-pull cadence (7d) cycles it.
findings.mechanism: price-only writes back old annual/timeseries arrays. computeCoverage measures presence on those persisted arrays -> reports unchanged coverage even after Yahoo stops supplying the field live. DROP_THRESHOLD never trips until full pulls cycle through.
findings.reproducer: Yahoo drops annualSGA live. For up to 7 days, price-only refreshes keep old annualSGA persisted; computeCoverage reports unchanged coverage; no drift alert until full pulls cycle.
findings.impact: Up to ~7-day blind window on fundamentals schema drift, masked by price-only persistence. Per-snapshot grade also frozen so it cannot reflect the drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Tag coverage-history entries with pullMode and compute drift coverage only over snapshots freshly fundamentals-pulled this run (status 'ok'); or maintain a separate fresh-fundamentals coverage series so price-only persistence does not dilute drift detection.

findings.title: data-quality-report scalar KEY_FIELDS use `.value != null`, diverging from grader's finite-number test
findings.description: _arrayElementPresent (line 43-49) was aligned with _arrLen for ARRAY fields, but the scalar metric checks in KEY_FIELDS still use `s.metrics.X.value != null` (marketCap, revenueTTM, grossMargin, operatingMargin, fcfMarginTTM, forwardPE, insiderOwner). The grader's _hasMetric requires Number.isFinite(value) and rejects non-numeric strings ('N/A') and NaN. The report therefore counts a value:'N/A' or value:NaN field as present while the grader counts it missing - the same inconsistency Tag 232c-23 claimed to close, fixed only for array fields.
findings.mechanism: `!= null` passes NaN and the string 'N/A'. _hasMetric rejects both. Report coverage % overstates relative to grade distribution for any field Yahoo returns as 'N/A'/NaN.
findings.reproducer: Snapshot with metrics.forwardPE.value=NaN -> report KEY_FIELDS forwardPE counts present (NaN != null); gradeSnapshot._hasMetric counts missing. Report shows higher coverage than grade distribution implies.
findings.impact: Operator-facing report disagrees with the actual grader on per-field coverage - the exact confusion Tag 232c-23 set out to eliminate. Reporting-trust issue, low corruption risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Export _hasMetric from methods/data-quality.js and reuse it for scalar KEY_FIELDS so report and grader share one definition of metric presence.

findings.title: Coverage tracker omits several consumed metrics (analyst targets, ROE/ROA, EV ratios, sharesOutstanding)
findings.description: TRACKED_FIELDS was extended for Tag 211l/219/220c, but fields now populated by the mapper and consumed by methods remain untracked: metrics.targetMeanPrice (analyst-upside), metrics.returnOnEquity/returnOnAssets, metrics.enterpriseToEbitda/enterpriseToRevenue, metrics.debtToEquity/currentRatio/quickRatio, external.earningsHistory, and meta.sharesOutstanding (buyback-yield fallback). If Yahoo stops supplying any of these, drift detection stays silent because the field is not enumerated.
findings.mechanism: computeCoverage only iterates TRACKED_FIELDS; un-enumerated fields are never measured so a deprecation is invisible - same class as the F-DQ-002 HIGH that Tag 232c-31 fixed for the 211l/219/220c block.
findings.reproducer: Yahoo drops financialData.targetMeanPrice -> analyst-upside methods degrade, but no coverage entry exists so detectDrift never fires.
findings.impact: Blind spots in schema-drift detection for ~10 actively consumed fields; each is a future silent-degradation candidate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the consumed fields to TRACKED_FIELDS (at minimum targetMeanPrice.value, returnOnEquity.value, enterpriseToEbitda.value, meta.sharesOutstanding).

findings.title: Large-scale FX fallback (stale 2024 rates) has no run-level alarm threshold
findings.description: loadFx() reverts per-currency stale rates to FX_FALLBACK (the hardcoded 2024 table) and tags per-snapshot fxRateSource='hardcoded-fallback', logging staleCount via console.log only. There is no run-level gate that HIGH-alerts when a large fraction of the universe ends up on fallback rates. A multi-week refresh-fx outage silently prices entire EM/UK legs off 2024 rates with only INFO/WARN logs.
findings.mechanism: console.log/console.warn are informational; no counter feeds the alert pipeline; nothing aggregates the count of snapshots carrying fxRateSource='hardcoded-fallback'.
findings.reproducer: Stop refresh-fx for 30 days; majors+EM revert to fallback; pull logs INFO lines; no HIGH alert; all non-USD ratios drift with stale 2024 FX.
findings.impact: Slow systematic mispricing of non-USD tickers during FX-refresh outages goes unalarmed; magnitude = drift between 2024 hardcoded rate and live rate (>20% for some EM ccys).
findings.suggested_fix: Count snapshots/currencies on hardcoded-fallback per run; emit a HIGH alert when the fallback ratio exceeds a threshold, mirroring field-coverage drift alerts.

findings.title: Dead _convertToUSD helper fails open on unknown currency
findings.description: _convertToUSD(value,currency) returns the raw value unchanged when no FX rate exists (rate==null), with no flag. No callers were found (dead code), and the live snapshot path (_convertSnapshotToUSD) correctly fail-closes via fxConversionFailed. The standalone helper is a latent fail-open footgun if ever wired in.
findings.mechanism: rate==null -> return value (no scaling, no failure marker). A caller would treat local-ccy as USD.
findings.reproducer: _convertToUSD(1000,'KZT') with KZT absent from FX_TO_USD -> returns 1000 unconverted, no signal.
findings.impact: Currently inert (unused). Latent silent-corruption shape; recommend deletion or fail-closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete unused _convertToUSD, or return a sentinel on missing rate so it cannot fail open.
